answer_sql:
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE
      trading_state = 'active' AND sales_lines = 0) > 0
    THEN 'yes'
    ELSE 'no'
  END AS answer_trading_shops,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE
    sales_lines = 0) > 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS answer_including_closed,
  COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE
    trading_state = 'active') AS trading_shops_checked,
  COUNT(*) AS all_italian_shops_checked,
  MIN(sales_lines) FILTER(WHERE
    trading_state = 'active') AS fewest_sales_at_a_trading_shop,
  MIN(sales_lines) AS fewest_sales_at_any_italian_shop
FROM (
  SELECT
    s.store_key,
    CASE WHEN s.close_date IS NULL THEN 'active' ELSE 'closed' END AS trading_state,
    COUNT(f.order_key) AS sales_lines
  FROM contoso_served.dim_store AS s
  LEFT JOIN contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS f
    ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  WHERE
    s.location_code <> -1 AND s.country_code = 'IT'
  GROUP BY
    1,
    2
) AS t

body.value: One row holding the answer: no — there is no shop in Italy that has never recorded a sale. The evidence in the same row: 2 trading Italian shops examined and 3 counting the closed one, with the fewest sales standing at 1,983 sales lines for the quieter trading shop (Pesaro) and 115 for the closed Caltanissetta. Counted over the full ten years of order dates, 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31. The figure measures sales attributed to the shop the sale was rung up at; it says nothing about sales made to Italian customers at shops elsewhere, nothing about the 55 trading shops outside Italy, and nothing about whether these shops sold WELL — only that each of them sold.
